memory_update.text: TLN and CEG should remain priority candidates for the firm-power node because both have named hyperscaler nuclear PPAs tied to AWS or Meta data-center needs.

ETR is a high-relevance regional regulated-utility candidate because its Louisiana agreements and LPSC approvals are directly tied to Meta data-center load, new combined-cycle generation, substations, transmission, and gas transportation.
GEV and PWR are equipment/services chokepoint candidates rather than direct power purchasers; rank them by evidence of data-center-specific backlog and margin contribution.

For this node, signed PPAs, regulated cost recovery, interconnection approvals, substation/transmission awards, turbine slot reservations, and long-lead equipment procurement are stronger evidence than generic AI electricity demand commentary.

Further passes should test adjacent US-listed candidates not included due to the five-name limit: DTE, NEE, VST, SO, D, ET, BWXT, LEU, CCJ, NRG, and regulated transmission/electrical equipment suppliers.
